supersession_notice.reason_for_change: Revision 1 explicitly recorded (NB-08) that preflight_state.json had not been examined in depth and was assumed to carry no load-bearing claim. That assumption was wrong. On completing the deferred depth pass, preflight_state.json was found to be the canonical production governance document R2_STATE.md, whose ## Estado section states that the authorized next step is read-only preparation only and explicitly does not authorize ramas/PRs, and that any later execution or D mutation requires a new Human Gate D. The package contains no artifact evidencing that such a Human Gate D was granted for attempt 2, while every governance artifact it does contain declares execution NOT authorized. This is an authorization-chain evidence gap that a PASS would have carried into the canonical record.
supersession_notice.what_did_not_change: No technical finding from revision 1 was withdrawn. All integrity, capture, binding, mutation-surface, terminal-state and live-reobservation results stand unchanged and are restated below.
supersession_notice.self_criticism: Deferring a 98KB evidence object on the assumption that it was a secondary aggregate snapshot, and issuing a disposition before resolving it, was an error of audit sequencing on the reviewer's part. Load-bearing status must be established by reading the object, not by inferring it from filename and size.

blocking_findings.title: No Human Gate D authorization artifact for attempt 2 exists anywhere in the package, while every governance artifact the package does contain declares execution NOT authorized
evidence: preflight_state.json decodes to canonical production R2_STATE.md (70548 bytes, git blob sha1 d8e5c7796322c6ac60761dba3485f69d15debe6b, served from production main 5a5b4b1b..., last updated 2026-08-16T13:44:26Z). Its ## Estado 'Authorized next step' authorizes only read-only preparation and states verbatim that it does not authorize ramas/PRs, required checks, branch protection, rulesets, merge or settings, and that any later execution or D mutation requires a new Human Gate D.
The same document's ## Gate de fase records 'Gate de salida de R2-4: NOT_EXECUTED' and 'Siguiente fase permitida: NO'.

The in-package runner-candidate independent review declares candidate_execution_authorized=false, execution_authority=NONE, required_changes_before_execution_Human_Gate_D=[] and new_Human_Gate_D_required_before_any_execution=true.

That same review summarises HUMAN_GATE_SCOPE.json (1254 bytes) as declaring candidate_execution_authority NONE and listing candidate execution, network use, GitHub mutation, opening PR #2, token or PEM use, production or PR #6 mutation, reopening PR #1 and L2 as not authorized. HUMAN_GATE_SCOPE.json itself is not present in this package.

The runner does implement a technical gate — exact argv with self SHA and runner-review SHA, plus environment variable R2_V14_V2_ATTEMPT2_HUMAN_GATE_D set to a fixed value — and execution demonstrably satisfied it. But the package contains no invocation record, no environment attestation, no signed or hashed authorization artifact, and no dated Human Gate D decision naming attempt 2.
R2_STATE.md mentions the laboratory repository, the V13/V14 lab series, LAB-ID-OBSERVATION and id-observation zero times, so the canonical record neither authorizes the lab work nor acknowledges it.
blocking_findings.why_this_blocks: The review request's PASS rule requires that mutation scope be exact and that no absent or ambiguous observation be promoted to PASS. Whether the observed mutation was inside an approved scope cannot be answered from the package bytes: the approval artifact is absent, and the only governance text present points the other way. Canonicalization writes into that same canonical record, so admitting an unevidenced authorization at this gate is the specific failure mode the apparatus exists to prevent.
blocking_findings.why_this_is_not_BLOCKED_INVALID: There is no unsafe completed mutation, no false green, no merge, no production or PR #6 drift, no cleanup, no L2 start, no credential exposure and no unclassifiable terminal state. The mutation was confined to a disposable laboratory repository and terminated CLOSED_UNMERGED. The gap is documentary, not operational.
blocking_findings.required_change: Supply the Human Gate D authorization artifact that authorized attempt 2 — hash- and byte-identified, naming the exact lab repository, PR #2, the two App check-run surfaces and the two installation-token mints, and dated between the runner-candidate review (2026-08-19T00:00:00Z) and execution start (2026-08-19T19:54:25Z) — together with HUMAN_GATE_SCOPE.json in full, and a reconciliation note explaining the relationship between that gate and the read-only 'Authorized next step' line standing in R2_STATE.md at production main 5a5b4b1b.... If such an artifact exists and reconciles, every other criterion for EVIDENCE_PASS is already met and this review converts to PASS on documentary review alone.

evidence_disposition_reason: Package integrity is complete and recomputed from bytes at every level, all 21 raw captures validate on every dimension, and every technical claim in the RESULT was re-derived from lower-level evidence and independently reobserved live with exact matches: single PR open with exact BASE and HEAD, exact refs/pull/2/merge acquisition with parents ordered [BASE, HEAD], native binding to PR_HEAD with three check-runs there and zero on TEST_MERGE, empty commit-status surfaces, lab-scoped minimal tokens with no credential material in the package, zero rulesets before during after and now, CLOSED_UNMERGED terminal state, PR #1 untouched, and production main, PR #6, lab main, all 61 lab heads and the tag set unchanged. Nothing technical is missing and no false green was created. What is missing is documentary: the package contains no artifact evidencing the Human Gate D that authorized attempt 2 to mutate anything, while the canonical production state it carries authorizes only read-only preparation and explicitly excludes branches and PRs, and the in-package runner review declares execution not authorized and a new Human Gate D required. Canonicalization writes into that canonical record, so the authorization must be evidenced before the record is written. This is a single, closable documentary gap requiring no re-execution.
